On 1 October 2026 the Mossos d'Esquadra arrested seven men, aged 29 to 55,
suspected of links to a drug-trafficking organisation. The operation took
place in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, where officers seized 8,025
kg of hashish. The investigation began in June 2026, after Mossos stopped a
van carrying about 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, Barcelona.

Surveillance in early October showed repeated movements of people and vans and
the arrival of an articulated lorry. Inside the warehouse, officers found
seven people unloading pallets from the trailer, intending to load the hashish
into several vans for distribution. The pallets held hashish hidden among
the goods. The drug was inside large raffia sacks filled with rubber chips,
a method used to make detection at police or customs checks harder.
Officers also found a firearm in one of the arrested men's vans.

The hashish is worth more than €16.2 million on the illicit market. The 8
tonnes are a significant part of the hashish the Mossos seized in 2026, which
reached about 14,900 kg up to 1 October. The seven men were placed at the
disposal of the civil and investigating section of the Figueres court of first
instance. The investigation remains open, and further arrests are not ruled
out.

The National Police arrested four men and a woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a drug-trafficking group, and seized 60 kilos of hashish and
weapons. The Grupo I de Estupefacientes ended an investigation that had
begun months earlier with five arrests.

Officers intercepted a package containing 24 kilos of hashish addressed to a man
living in Palma, and arrested him on suspicion of drug trafficking. In the
first home, that of the main suspect, officers found 36 kilos of hashish, an air
rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested a man and a
woman.

In the second home, officers found two kilos of cocaine, doses, a cutting
substance, a pistol with nine-millimetre cartridges, a bow with arrows and a
hydraulic press, and arrested a second suspect who allegedly guarded and
transported drugs. A fifth person was arrested for being linked to the
case. Police suspect the drug was distributed to third parties for
small-scale sale, the investigation remains open, and further arrests are not
ruled out.

A 24-year-old mainland man arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, on the
night of 4 November. During customs clearance in the early hours of 5
November, Customs officers found suspected cannabis buds in his carry-on
baggage. He was then arrested.

Customs said it seized about 9 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds, with an
estimated market value of about $1.9 million, in a drug trafficking case
involving baggage concealment. Chinese-language outlet Dot Dot News
reported the same 9 kilograms and an estimated value of HK$1.9 million. The
arrested man has been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The case was due at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 6 November.

Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a
serious offence. The maximum penalty on conviction is a fine of $5 million
and life imprisonment.
